# zidl — Java Backend Reference

Generated by `zidl -b java`. Produces `.java` source files with generated schema traversal
and a dependency on the pure-Java `zidl-cdr-java` JAR for shared codec helpers. Follows the IDL4-to-Java
mapping (formal/21-08-01 v1.0).

---

## Generated Files

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `Types.java` | All types from the IDL (default single-file mode) |

With `--split-files`, one `.java` file is produced per top-level named type, named
after the type (e.g. `MyStruct.java`, `MyEnum.java`), plus a shared
`<Stem>CdrUtils.java` for that IDL input. With `--java-package`, helpers share the
types' package. Without it, types stay in the default package and helpers use
`zidl.generated`, allowing legal static imports. Compile all generated sources
with `javac -d <classes> ...` so javac creates the package directories. See the
[output-mode checkpoint](design/java-cdr-output-parity.md).

---

## Type Mapping

| IDL type | Java type |
|---|---|
| `boolean` | `boolean` |
| `octet` | `byte` |
| `char` | `char` |
| `wchar` | `char` |
| `short` / `int16` | `short` |
| `unsigned short` / `uint16` | `short` |
| `long` / `int32` | `int` |
| `unsigned long` / `uint32` | `int` |
| `long long` / `int64` | `long` |
| `unsigned long long` / `uint64` | `long` |
| `float` | `float` |
| `double` | `double` |
| `long double` | `double` |
| `fixed<D,S>` | `double` (approximate, using the same packed-BCD helpers in both modes) |
| `string` / `wstring` | `String` |
| `sequence<T>` | `java.util.List<T>` (an `ArrayList`); a sequence of an array typedef is `List<int[]>` etc. |
| `T[N]` | `T[]` |
| `map<K,V>` | `java.util.Map<K, V>` |
| `@optional T` | nullable field (`T` reference, default `null`) |
| `enum` | Java `enum` with `int value` field and `fromValue(int)` factory |
| `bitmask` | `int` (`long` above `@bit_bound(32)`), with a constants class of flag values |
| `bitset` | Java `class` with integer storage field |
| `struct` | Java `class` (private fields with `get_*`/`set_*`, default/copy constructors) |
| `union` | Java `class` with discriminant field + typed case methods |
| IDL module | Nested namespace class in single-file output; split types are top-level under `--java-package` |

---

Enums and bitmasks are encoded in 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes by `@bit_bound` (default 32),
matching the other backends and XTypes. An array of an array typedef is one
multi-dimensional Java array (`Triple a[2]` with `typedef long Triple[3]` is
`int[2][3]`); an array of sequences uses a raw `java.util.List[]`, since Java cannot
create generic arrays.

## Generated File Structure

Single-file output wraps IDL types in an outer class named after the input stem.
For a top-level `Sample` in `model.idl`:

```java
package com.example; // --java-package com.example

public class Model {
    // Private static _cdr* helper methods occur once in this outer class.
    public static class Sample implements java.io.Serializable {
        private int x;
        private String name = "";

        public int get_x() { return x; }
        public void set_x(int value) { x = value; }
        public String get_name() { return name; }
        public void set_name(String value) { name = value; }

        // Constructors, codec and optional key methods are generated here.
    }
}
```

Split-file types are top-level classes and import the public static helpers
from `<Stem>CdrUtils`. Alignment and narrow-string helpers forward to `io.zidl.cdr.Cdr`; other helpers
remain generated in this first extraction. Put the matching `zidl-cdr-java` JAR
on both compilation and runtime classpaths. `--no-typesupport` output and older
inline generated sources remain runtime-free. There are no `ZidlCdrWriter`/`ZidlCdrReader` helper classes.

Build the JAR with `zig build java-runtime` or the standalone Python/JDK build
in [packages/zidl-cdr-java](../packages/zidl-cdr-java/README.md). Source and JAR
release artifacts require no C/Zig compiler for Java consumption. For example:

```sh
javac -encoding UTF-8 -cp zidl-cdr-java.jar -d classes generated/*.java MyApp.java
java -cp classes:zidl-cdr-java.jar MyApp
```

Use `;` in place of `:` on Windows. Generated helpers require Java runtime API 1;
see the [first extraction checkpoint](design/java-cdr-extraction-1.md).

## CDR Serialize/Deserialize Signatures

Representative methods on a generated type:

```java
public void serialize(java.nio.ByteBuffer buf, int cdrBase, int xcdrVersion);
public static Sample deserializeFrom(java.nio.ByteBuffer buf, int cdrBase, int xcdrVersion);
public static void skip(java.nio.ByteBuffer buf, int cdrBase, int xcdrVersion);
```

The buffer position supplies the current cursor, while `cdrBase` supplies the
alignment origin (normally 4 after an encapsulation header). Ordinary generated
methods set little-endian byte order. Supported version/shape combinations and
known validation gaps are inventoried in the [audit](design/java-cdr-audit.md).

---

## Key Serialization

For structs with `@key` members:

```java
public void serializeKeyHolder(java.nio.ByteBuffer buf, int cdrBase);
public void serializeKey(java.nio.ByteBuffer buf, int cdrBase, int xcdrVersion);
public static Sample deserializeKey(java.nio.ByteBuffer buf, int cdrBase, int xcdrVersion);
public byte[] computeKeyHash();
public static byte[] computeKeyHashFromCdr(byte[] payload);
public static byte[] computeKeyHashFromCdrKeyOnly(byte[] payload);
```

`serializeKeyHolder` emits canonical big-endian PLAIN_CDR2 holder bytes, without
encapsulation. Wire key methods retain their version-specific framing.
`computeKeyHash` uses the declared maximum key size to select padding or MD5;
an unbounded key type or a maximum above 16 forces MD5 even for short values.
The incoming full-sample and key-only entry points accept their respective
encapsulated wire shapes and derive the same canonical holder hash.

MD5 uses `java.security.MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")` — no external dependency.

---

## `--generate-interfaces` and JNI

When `--generate-interfaces` is set, each IDL `interface` declaration produces a
`*Impl.java` class that loads a native JNI library:

```java
public class FooImpl {
    static {
        System.loadLibrary("my_dds_lib");   // from --java-jni-library my_dds_lib
    }
    // native method declarations
}
```

Pass the library name with `--java-jni-library <name>`.

---

## Backend-Specific Options

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--java-package <pkg>` | Java package for generated types (e.g. `com.example`) |
| `--split-files` | One `.java` file per top-level type |
| `--java-jni-library <name>` | `System.loadLibrary()` name for `--generate-interfaces` JNI bridge |
| `--no-typesupport` | Suppress CDR serialize/deserialize output |

---

## Integration Test

The Java integration test in `test/integration/java/Test.java` compiles against the
committed golden `test/golden/java/Types.java` using `javac` and runs with `java`.
Zig's build system automatically skips the Java tests if `javac`/`java` is not on `PATH`.

Run directly:

```sh
zig build integration-test   # runs all integration tests including Java if javac found
```

---

## Known Limitations

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| `any` / `object` / `value_base` member access | Emits `// TODO: any/object` comment |
